answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit work, with rewards released only after independent peers verify the result. Creating a hundred identities then does not multiply influence for free: each must tie up capital, and a proven fraudulent submission burns its bond. This makes a sybil campaign costly to scale and exposes attackers to losses, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright. A spiral of repeated checks can help peers catch coordinated fraud; raven and mesa can be ordinary agent names, not proof of distinct people.
